transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-03 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Jenna (Polaris Search Eng), Tom (CTO), Laila (Product), Samir (Eng)

Summary (auto): quick run through of embeddings + rerank APIs, walked sample queries, showed Console rerank dashboard and Optimize suggestions. Action items captured.

[00:00:08] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE on the account. Carlos from our SE team will run through the demo today. um quick intro from your side?
[00:00:18] Jenna (Polaris): hi, this is Jenna, search eng on Polaris. we're looking to improve search relevance on marketplace listing results, currently using a tf-idf + light boosting layer.
[00:00:23] Tom (Polaris): Tom here, CTO — mostly listening but want to see cost/scale numbers.
[00:00:27] Maya: great. Carlos, over to you.
[00:00:30] Carlos (Redwood): cool yeah thanks. i'll start with a quick architecture slide — apologies if the slide text is small, i'm sharing my screen now. so at a high level, hosted API gives you embeddings endpoint and a separate rerank endpoint. typical flow: 1) embed customer query + candidate docs, 2) initial vector retrieval, 3) rerank with our rerank API which internally calls the model with full context and returns scores.
[00:01:12] Jenna: do you require storing vectors in your system or do we push them to our own vector DB?
[00:01:18] Carlos: good q. you can do either. hosted mode you can store vectors in your vector DB — we generally see customers using their own vector store (pinecone, milvus, etc) and calling our embeddings endpoint to encode items at ingest. we also offer a managed index add-on but that's separate.
[00:01:40] Laila: what about freshness? our listings update quickly, so latency on indexing matters.
[00:01:46] Carlos: embeddings endpoint is synchronous and fast — we optimize batching. typical single-item embed latency is ~30-60ms on our recommended models, and you can batch to amortize cost. we also provide incremental embed pipelines in the console.
[00:02:15] Samir: what's the rerank model doing differently vs just dot-product scoring?
[00:02:20] Carlos: rerank takes the top-k candidates and runs a contextual scoring pass — it sees query + doc text, does cross-attention, and outputs a relevance score. that helps reorder by semantic match and signals like intent.
[00:02:39] [00:02:41] Jenna: any gotchas with snippet length or token limits?
[00:02:44] Carlos: yes, token budget matters — rerank works best when documents are clipped to important sections. we showed an example where we sent title + first 300 chars. for long product descriptions we recommend summary fields or storing embeddings of passages.
[00:03:05] Maya: i'll show Console now — per-route latency & token cost. Carlos, can you demo Optimize suggestions?
[00:03:12] Carlos: sure, switching to Console. so here's a per-route dashboard — you can filter to the rerank route, see P50/P95 latencies, and token cost breakdown by request. Optimize then analyzes your traffic shape and suggests batching parameters, cache TTLs for common prefixes, and a quantization profile if you want to reduce GPU cost.
[00:03:45] Tom: quantization — are there quality tradeoffs?
[00:03:48] Carlos: there can be, but for rerank we often recommend int8 profiles that preserve rank ordering for most queries. we also link to evals so you can run your test prompts against quantized variants.
[00:04:10] Jenna: can you show an example rerank call payload?
[00:04:14] Carlos: yep — here's the JSON: query, candidates (text + metadata), and a config block (candidate_limit, score_threshold). returns candidate array with scores and explanation snippets. i'll paste sample in chat.
[00:04:35] [00:04:37] Samir: any rate limits on rerank? we want to run 100k scoring requests per minute at peak.
[00:04:43] Carlos: hosted plans have soft rate limits; for that scale you'd look at Dedicated capacity — we can size a reserved pool for predictable throughput. hosted can burst but you may see throttling if peaks are sustained.
[00:05:05] Laila: what's typical cost delta between hosted vs dedicated?
[00:05:09] Maya: quickballpark: hosted is pay-per-use and good for pilots; dedicated is a monthly commitment that lowers per-token unit cost and gives capacity guarantees. we'll send a three-tier estimate like we mentioned.
[00:05:30] Jenna: security — we have to comply with SOC2 and want SSO and audit logs. what's supported?
[00:05:36] Maya: we support SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs in Console, and SOC2 documentation — we'll share the pack. for stricter data controls you can use Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which keeps inference in your VPC.
[00:05:58] Tom: good. do you support KMS/HSM for keys?
[00:06:02] Carlos: yes — integrations with major KMS + HSM options; we'll include config notes.
[00:06:12] [00:06:15] Carlos: ok demo time — i'm going to run an end-to-end example. sample dataset is marketplace subset. first step: embed query 'men's waterproof hiking boots' and show top candidates via vector store.
[00:06:30] [00:06:32] Carlos: embedding call returns vector in 45ms (demo latency noisy because screen share), then rerank call with top-20 returns ranked list, score delta shows that items with updated shipping tags bumped up.
[00:06:58] Jenna: wow, can you show the explanation snippet?
[00:07:01] Carlos: yep — our rerank response includes a short explanation field (auto-generated) like 'matches product features: waterproof; matches [query intent: hiking]'. it's heuristic but helps debug.
[00:07:22] Samir: is explanation produced by the model or a rules layer?
[00:07:26] Carlos: mostly model-generated with templating to keep it stable.
[00:07:35] [00:07:37] Laila: what about A/B testing or rollouts? can we run canary rerank models?
[00:07:41] Carlos: yes — Console supports rollouts: you can route X% to a variant model, monitor per-route metrics, and auto-fallback to baseline if quality drops. we also integrate evals to run your labeled prompts.
[00:08:00] Jenna: any recommendations for candidate K (top-k) size?
[00:08:03] Carlos: usually top-10 to top-50 depending on precision/latency tradeoff. more candidates increases rerank cost linearly. Optimize can suggest a sweet spot based on your traffic.
[00:08:25] Tom: what's the common architecture for cold-start items? we have lots of new SKUs.
[00:08:30] Carlos: many customers queue new items for immediate embedding at upload time; you can also use a fast lightweight model to create provisional embeddings and then re-embed with larger model later.
[00:08:46] [00:09:00] Maya: quick pause — any blockers or must-have features for you? Jenna?
[00:09:06] Jenna: hard requirement is <120ms p95 end-to-end rerank latency for product search. also strong interest in preserving merchant-level boosts.
[00:09:17] Carlos: doable with Dedicated capacity and optimized batching — we'll document a config for p95 targets.
[00:09:25] Samir: curious about CVR impact — do you have case studies?
[00:09:30] Maya: we have a couple anonymized case studies where semantic rerank improved click-through / conversion by 6–12% for marketplace customers — i'll link in the follow-up.
[00:09:47] Laila: how do we tune for merch boosts — do you feed merchant weight as a feature to rerank?
[00:09:52] Carlos: yes you can pass metadata features per candidate (merchant_priority, promo flags) and the model factors them into the score. you can also apply post-score multipliers in your application if you want hard constraints.
[00:10:10] [00:10:12] Carlos: switching to Optimize tab — here it analyzed a week's traffic, suggesting batch size 8, prefix cache TTL 45s for a common query, and recommending a quantized model variant for rerank that cuts cost by ~30% with minimal PR degrade.
[00:10:43] Jenna: does Optimize automatically apply changes or just recommend?
[00:10:46] Carlos: recommend only, we leave rollout decisions to you. but we can auto-apply safe batch-size increases if you opt in.
[00:10:55] Tom: what's the SLA on hosted?
[00:10:58] Maya: hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated includes SLA-backed throughput and latency targets. exact numbers in the enterprise pack — we'll include in follow-up.
[00:11:15] Jenna: sample telemetry — can we get token-level cost by route?
[00:11:19] Carlos: yes Console shows token counts, unit costs, and p95 by route.
[00:11:27] [00:11:33] Carlos: quick live debug — i'm going to show rerank with merchant boost set to 1.5, then 0.8, watch positions change.
[00:11:48] [00:11:55] Jenna: that worked. interesting to see subtle reorder.
[00:12:00] Laila: what about monitoring for quality regressions after model updates?
[00:12:04] Carlos: Console supports eval-based monitors — you provide a prompt set and expected labels; we run daily checks and alert on regression. can tie to rollout policy to halt canaries.
[00:12:20] Samir: ok what's needed from our side to run a pilot?
[00:12:23] Maya: sample dataset, headcount for integration (1-2 engs), and success metrics (CTR, p95 latency). we'll provision a sandbox key and a small hosted credit to run experiments.
[00:12:37] Jenna: timeline — we want a pilot in 2–3 weeks if we can get sandbox and a quickstart.
[00:12:43] Maya: noted. we'll aim for that.
[00:12:47] [00:12:50] Carlos: last bit — tradeoffs recap: hosted = fast onboarding, pay-as-you-go; dedicated = lower unit cost + predictable capacity + SLA; private = full control for compliance.
[00:13:08] Tom: nice summary. any immediate risks? Jenna: only if latency targets aren't met.
[00:13:15] Maya: we'll run a benchmark plan and share results before pilot kickoff.
[00:13:22] Laila: ok sounds good.
[00:13:25] Maya: cool. i'll send the security pack, quickstart repos, and pricing tiers. Carlos will follow up on benchmarks. any final q's?
[00:13:36] Jenna: none right now. thanks everyone.
[00:13:40] Tom: thanks.
[00:13:41] Maya: thanks all — end call.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcribed, occasional mis-hears for product names and tokens; timestamps approximate.
